messages.subject: Multi-group analysis error?
parts:
Hi, 

I am trying to run a multi-group analysis. There are three groups in my data. The standardized regression estimates for Group 1 and 3 seems fine, but then Group 2 doesn't seem right. 

This is my code: 

model.2 <-  'PA =~ PA.1 + PA.2 + PA.3 
RE =~ RE.1 + RE.2 + RE.3 
PD =~ PD.1 + PD.2 + PD.3
GD =~ GD.1 + GD.2 + GD.3
G_IN =~ G_IN.1 + G_IN.2 + G_IN.3 + G_IN.4
POS.WORDS =~ Joyful + Happy + Enjoyment + Pleased + Fun 
POS.WORDS ~ PA + RE + PD + GD + G_IN + Age + Sex + Education + Income + Neuroticism'

fit.2 <- cfa(model.2, data= Multi.group, group='Group')
summary(fit.2, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)


Results for group 2

Regressions:
  POS.WORDS ~
    PA                2.657    3.432    0.774    0.439    2.380    2.380
    RE                0.467    1.005    0.465    0.642    0.470    0.470
    PD               -2.380    3.570   -0.667    0.505   -1.295   -1.295
    GD                0.307    0.621    0.495    0.621    0.254    0.254
    G_IN             -0.929    2.196   -0.423    0.672   -0.986   -0.986
    Age               0.003    0.005    0.644    0.519    0.004    0.037
    Sex               0.133    0.105    1.262    0.207    0.149    0.073
    Education        -0.101    0.042   -2.396    0.017   -0.114   -0.141
    Income            0.001    0.043    0.028    0.978    0.001    0.002
    Neuroticism       0.003    0.065    0.042    0.967    0.003    0.002

I am not quite sure why PA and PD would have estimates above 1 and below 0 respectively. I would appreciate some help. 

The item estimates for each trait is similar across all three groups, but my interest is with the structural part of the model. Only group 2 is exhibiting this strangeness. 

Thank you. 
Sam.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Multi-group analysis error?
parts:
It's unusual but it is not impossible. It happens because the variables are highly correlated (and it happens in regression, which is easier to understand because it doensn't have all the additional complexity of SEM. The standard reference for SEM is this:

http://www.ssicentral.com/lisrel/techdocs/HowLargeCanaStandardizedCoefficientbe.pdf

Here's a regression example:



> set.seed(1234)
> x1 <- scale(rnorm(1000))
> y <- scale(rnorm(1000)/10 + x1^3.1 + x1 )
> x2 <- scale(x1^2)
> x3 <- scale(x1^3)
> summary(lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3))


Coefficients:
Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) -0.668816 0.010877 -61.490 <2e-16 ***
x1 0.262826 0.009678 27.157 <2e-16 ***
x2 -0.129514 0.013084 -9.899 <2e-16 ***
x3 1.156142 0.009064 127.553 <2e-16 ***
